answer: Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 26% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Because the grove ordering is published with the river batch, the nadir audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early thus gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. A 278 account operation therefore ties up 9 million dollars of idle capital. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
